reviews.source: StraySpark blog: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Windsurf for Unreal Engine
reviews.summary: Months of UE5 C++ use with all three tools. Claude Code was the main recommendation for MCP-driven editor automation and multi-file refactors (first-try compile in 7 of 10 runs of an inventory-component refactor). Downsides: no built-in IntelliSense, slower startup and higher daily token cost.

reviews.source: StraySpark blog: Cursor 3 vs Claude Code for UE5 Development
reviews.summary: Based on the studio's own UE 5.7 use, no measurements. Claude Code is preferred for large existing C++ codebases, consistent refactors, long builds and MCP; neither tool can edit Blueprint .uasset files. Recommends using both tools.

vendorClaims.text: Default model is Opus 5.5 on Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise and API; Fable must be picked explicitly.

strengths: top of every product-level agent board found (Terminal-Bench 4.0, AA Coding Agent Index, GameDevBench Godot, GameEngineBench UE5)
reliable multi-file C++ refactors and deep MCP/editor automation (StraySpark)
fastest and most polished in Ars one-shot game test
weaknesses: higher per-task cost (AA: ~$11.42/task with Opus 5.5; StraySpark: $25-40/day on Opus)
can't edit Blueprint .uasset; weak at generating Unity scene layouts

reviews.source: StraySpark blog: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Windsurf for Unreal Engine
reviews.summary: Cursor had the most polished UE IntelliSense (clangd), UE-aware tab completion and the best diff review. Its Composer refactors were ragged and missed call sites, it needs a hand-maintained .cursorignore, and MCP setup is fiddlier. Best for VS Code teams and small surgical edits.

reviews.source: StraySpark blog: Cursor 3 vs Claude Code for UE5 Development
reviews.summary: Cursor 3's parallel agents suit many independent edits, greenfield work and Slate/UMG iteration, but parallelism doesn't help with sequential UE compiles. Composer 2 trailed Claude on UE reflection code (UPROPERTY/UCLASS).

vendorClaims.text: Auto has Cost, Balance and Intelligence modes; individual plans get Cost mode, which bills as a Cursor-model request.

strengths: best UE IntelliSense, tab completion and diff review UI (StraySpark)
parallel agents for many independent edits (StraySpark)
free plan / familiar VS Code base
weaknesses: multi-file refactors miss call sites in UE C++ (StraySpark)
own Composer model mid-table on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (Vals #41/76)
billing and usage-limit complaints dominate Trustpilot

vendorClaims.text: Agent mode runs locally, in Copilot CLI or as a cloud coding agent; Auto model selection includes Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 models.

strengths: fast inline completions for boilerplate (Product Hunt reviewers)
widest IDE coverage; access to frontier Claude and GPT models via Auto
weaknesses: confident but wrong suggestions / invented APIs (PH, Unity forum)
weaker on large multi-file tasks than Cursor or Claude Code (PH reviewers)
github-copilot.note: No benchmark tests Copilot as a product; it picks among several models, so model-only leaderboard results aren't credited.

reviews.source: StraySpark blog: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Windsurf for Unreal Engine
reviews.summary: Windsurf's aggressive indexing and autonomous Cascade runs were strong and it was cheapest. But first indexing of a UE project took 15-45 min with heavy RAM, completion was less UE-aware, large refactors cascaded into errors and MCP felt bolted on. Suited to solo devs on a budget.

vendorClaims.text: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf; plans and pricing unchanged; 'Fusion' pairs a lead model with a SWE-2 sidekick.

strengths: strong autonomous agent runs and semantic indexing (StraySpark)
lowest cost of the IDE options (StraySpark)
weaknesses: slow first index and heavy RAM on UE projects (StraySpark)
windsurf.note: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (Cognition). The #2 Artificial Analysis result belongs to Cognition's Devin Fusion CLI, not the IDE, so it isn't counted.

reviews.source: Darko Unity blog: Unity AI Assistant review: not ready for real work
reviews.summary: Open-beta test: a one-prompt world-generation benchmark stalled at layer 2, another build hung on 'Preparing' for over 4,500 s, and a drivable-car script failed with bad colliders. Verdict: not ready for production work. Notes the assistant used Gemini 2.0 Flash for tool calling.

vendorClaims.text: Unity AI isn't trained on your code or data by default; open beta for all Unity 6 users from May 2026.

strengths: native editor integration and engine knowledge
useful for debugging, profiling and project audits (forum users)
weaknesses: unreliable on multi-step tasks; stalls and makes unrequested changes
setup and connection breakage (MCP, relay, BYO keys)

vendorClaims.text: Up to 10x faster and 6x cheaper than a standard MCP setup (self-measured on Ludus 1.0, 4 tasks, Sept 2026); syncs Blueprints, C++, assets and levels live; UE 5.4-5.8.
Calls itself the most comprehensive AI copilot for Unreal, with 1,655 native tools; works with hosted AI, your own keys or local LLMs.

notes: Missing tools to consider: Bezi, Coplay / Unity MCP bridges, JetBrains AI / Junie (Rider), Google Antigravity CLI / Gemini CLI, Meta Muse Code, OpenCode / Kimi Code (open, low-cost harnesses), Devin Fusion CLI (Cognition), Godot-specific assistants (Ziva, Summer Engine)
